sections.h2: What should a seller know about Putnam County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Putnam County has 23,722 residents by the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, up 7.6% from the 2020 base of 22,043. The city of Eatonton sets its own millage rate alongside the county, the school board and the state, so a bill can include several taxing bodies.

The county spreads across 344.68 square miles of land, with 64.0 people per square mile in 2020. Older residents are a large share: 27.1% of the population is 65 or older, and 31.1% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Retail activity is strong for the county's size, with 2022 retail sales of $321,128,000, which is $14,003 per resident.

Homes here mostly belong to their occupants. The owner-occupied rate is 80.9%, and 90.7% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. A listing in Putnam County tends to compete with long-held houses rather than recent flips.

sections.h2: What do Putnam County housing numbers show?
sections.html:
The 2020-2024 median value of an owner-occupied Putnam home is $249,300, sitting between Polk and Pike in the same Census table.

The gap between 14,017 housing units and 10,435 occupied households is large. Roughly 3,600 units are not counted as occupied households, which is a reminder that not every Putnam property carries a homestead exemption. Confirm with the assessor whether yours does before you estimate what the next owner will pay.

sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Putnam County?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner bills and collects, and the Board of Tax Assessors sets value. Keep the two straight and your calls go faster.

  • Tax Commissioner: collects property tax, timber tax and heavy duty equipment tax, and takes payments online, by phone, by mail or in the office.
  • Tax Assessor: (706) 485-6376, handles value, exemptions and appeals, and posts records at qpublic.net/ga/putnam.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: collects intangible tax and keeps deed copies in the Putnam County Courthouse.
  • City of Eatonton: adopts its own millage rate for property inside the city.

Georgia's Department of Revenue lists the county's tax commissioner website as putnamgatax.com. The office publishes a Taxpayer Brochure that covers returns, exemptions and appeals in more detail.

sections.h2: When is the Putnam County property tax bill due?
sections.html:
December 1 each year. Bills for real and personal property are generally mailed by October 1, and mobile home bills go out by February 1 with an April 1 due date.

Interest starts the day after the due date and is added again on the first day of every month until the bill is paid. The rate is the prime rate at the start of the year plus 3%. A 5% penalty follows at 120 days and grows by another 5% for each further 120 days, to a maximum of 20%. Mobile home penalties are 10%, charged the day after the due date.

Putnam stopped requiring mobile home decals after a resolution adopted July 2, 2021. Homestead property owing less than $500 is spared the 90-day penalty, per the office's FAQ, and tax bills never go to a mortgage company.

sections.h2: What happens when a Putnam County property is sold during the year?
sections.html:
The original bill still goes to whoever owned the property on January 1. Tax bills in Putnam County rest on ownership and value as of that date.

Once the new deed is recorded, the tax commissioner's office sends a copy of the bill to the buyer as well. The office tells readers to look at their closing documents or ask the closing attorney who owes the tax. In practice this means a seller should confirm that the settlement statement covers the year's bill, whether the sale happens before or after the December 1 due date.

Putnam also posts a second reminder for boat owners: a sold boat still produces a bill the following fall unless the assessor's marine equipment specialist hears about the sale.

sections.h2: How does a Putnam County appeal or exemption work?
sections.html:
Send a first appeal to the Board of Assessors. If they do not change the value again, the appeal is forwarded to the Board of Equalization, and you can choose an arbitrator instead within 45 days of the notice date. Superior Court is the last step.

  • Homestead: own and occupy the home on January 1, file at the assessor's office, and have it received before April 1.
  • Age: homeowners who reach 70 may apply for an additional homestead exemption.
  • Relief grant: the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant gave a one-time $18,000 assessed value reduction on 2023 homestead property, and the county says it is returning for tax year 2026.
  • Refunds: written requests for taxes wrongly collected must be started within three years of payment.

Rental and non-homesteaded property did not receive the grant, so landlords selling rentals should not expect that credit.

sections.h2: How is a Putnam County bill calculated and what does it pay for?
sections.html:
Assessed value is 40% of fair market value, and exemptions come off before the millage rate is applied. Putnam's rate is set by the Board of Commissioners, the Board of Education, the City of Eatonton and the State of Georgia. One mill is $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.

The county lists where the money goes: county government and the public schools, public buildings, bridges and county roads, courts, the jail and law enforcement, fire protection, and public health and sanitation. Returns for real estate go to the assessor's office between January 1 and April 1.

Boats are taxed only when the owner's marine equipment totals $20,000 or more, and the bill arrives with the fall property bills. Payment options include the website with cards or eChecks, the phone with cards, and the office with cash, cards or checks, with a processing fee on card payments.

sections.h2: What if a Putnam County tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
A tax FiFa (lien) can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court 30 days after the office sends a 30-day notice. The FAQ says an unpaid bill past 90 days can also reach credit bureaus through that public record.

The county generally holds one tax sale each year, on the first Tuesday in July at the courthouse. Bidders register in person with photo ID, there is no electronic bidding, and winners pay in certified funds the same day. Notices run in The Eatonton Messenger and on Georgia Public Notice.

Selling before that point is the cleaner option. Ask the tax commissioner for the payoff and the lien status, then have it paid at closing.

faqs.q: When are Putnam County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 1. The tax commissioner says bills are generally mailed by October 1, and mobile home bills are due April 1.

faqs.q: Does Putnam County hold a tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, generally one a year on the first Tuesday in July at the Putnam County Courthouse, with in-person bidding only and payment in certified funds.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax if I sell my Putnam County house mid-year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner of record is billed first, and the buyer gets a copy once the deed is recorded. Your closing documents and closing attorney settle who pays.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Putnam County?
faqs.a: Interest of prime plus 3% accrues, a 5% penalty applies at 120 days and each 120 days after that, up to 20%. Mobile homes carry a 10% penalty.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Putnam County tax assessor?
faqs.a: Call (706) 485-6376 for value, exemptions and appeals. Records are on qpublic.net/ga/putnam.
